why: The plan a delegate-build run consumes. Copy it, fill it, and let `delegate.plan` refuse it if a field is empty. The estate's rules are in the fields, not in the prose: prior_art says the work was not reinvented, staff_bar says the senior judgement was actually applied, skills says which packs the step leaned on, and done_check is the command that decides.

found: path -> the PR that added it

reuse: what existing code, PR or ticket this plan builds on

staff_bar.design_note: the decision, in one paragraph, and the alternative rejected
staff_bar.blast_radius: what else in the estate this touches, by path
staff_bar.rollback: how this is undone if it is wrong
staff_bar.observability: the log line, metric or surface that proves it works live
staff_bar.simplification: what was left out, and why that is enough

steps.title: one line
files: repo-relative paths this step may create or edit -- and nothing else
read: repo-relative paths the builder may read for context
skills: pack ids this step leans on, from `skill-packs.py list`
steps.instructions: exact change: signatures, message shapes, names, edge cases. No design left to the builder.
steps.done_check: shell command run from the repo root; exit 0 means the step is done (a real test that executes the new code)
